g.text: Two repos: APP REPO (gitops-apps) and GITOPS REPO (gitops-monorepo)
Application code and deployment config live in separate GitHub repos, owned by separate teams. The only bridge is one commit.
test -> e2e (kind, with the GitOps repo's chart) -> build + scan + sign -> deploy dev
does NOT contain: Helm chart, environments, ArgoCD, cluster credentials
# App repo: owned by the app team. Deployment config (Helm chart, environments, ArgoCD) is NOT here,
# it lives in the GitOps repo (github.com/rosaliei/gitops-monorepo), owned by the devops team.
THE ONLY BRIDGE between the two repos
# Write access to the GitOps repo = a deploy key (SSH) stored as secret GITOPS_DEPLOY_KEY.
# It can push to that ONE repo only: no API access, cannot open or merge PRs.
- name: deploy to dev = commit to the GitOps repo
images built by the app repo: ghcr.io/rosaliei/<app>:sha-xxxx | x.y.z
ONE shared Helm chart for every app
ci.yaml: validate + promtool + e2e (every change, also the bot's commits)
promotion-pr.yaml: promote/qa-* branch from the app repo -> qa PR
Where should the Helm chart live? and why two repos?
shared chart for every app = HOW apps run
B. In each app repo: when an app needs its own special chart
GitOps repo pins the version: many teams
1. permissions: devs merge code all day,
2. no CI loops: the bot's commits land in the other repo
3. clean deploy history: git log environments/
4. many app repos can feed one GitOps repo
"Developers own the code, devops owns how and where it runs.
The only bridge is a commit that changes an image tag,
and ArgoCD only ever reads the GitOps repo."
